body.name: \widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}
body.construction:
Suppose \(1<s\le2\), put \(m=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), and use the four deterministic folds \(F_j=\{(j-1)m+1,\ldots,jm\}\).  Set
\[
 H=\left(\frac{\kappa_n}{2^{12}M}\right)^{1/s}.
\]
For \(q\in[-1/2,1/2]\), let \(S_q(u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge q\}\), let \(\mathcal B_q=\operatorname{span}\{1,u,(u-q)_+\}\) in \(L^2[-1,1]\), and define
\[
 k_q=S_q-\Pi_{\mathcal B_q}S_q.
\]
For a fold \(j\), a center \(z\), a radius \(r\), and \(a=z+qr\), define
\[
 \widehat J_{j}(z,r,q)=
 \frac{1}{mr\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2}
 \sum_{i\in F_j}D_i k_q\!\left(\frac{X_i-z}{r}\right)
 \mathbf 1\{|X_i-z|\le r\}.
\]
On fold one, take centers on the \(H/8\)-mesh in \([1/4-H,3/4+H]\) and \(q\) on the \(\kappa_n/2^{16}\)-mesh in \([-1/2,1/2]\).  Retain every window \([z-H,z+H]\) for which \(\widehat J_1(z,H,q)\ge\kappa_n/2\) for at least one such \(q\), and let \(B=[A,B_+]\) be the connected hull of the retained windows, intersected with \([1/4-2H,3/4+2H]\).  If there is no retained window, return \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=1/2\).

Conditionally on fold one, fit by ordinary least squares on fold two a degree-one polynomial \(\widehat p_-\) over \([A-2H,A-H]\) and a degree-one polynomial \(\widehat p_+\) over \([B_++H,B_++2H]\), using on each flank the rescaled regressors \(1,(X-x_0)/H\), where \(x_0\) is that flank's left endpoint, and clip both fitted values to \([0,1]\).  The empirical Gram matrix is \(m^{-1}\sum_{i\in F_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i\text{ is in the flank}\}(1,(X_i-x_0)/H)^{\mathsf T}(1,(X_i-x_0)/H)\).  If either such \(2\times2\) matrix has smallest eigenvalue below \(H/48\), return \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=1/2\).  Otherwise, on the finite grid
\[
 \mathcal T_n=(n^{-1}\mathbb Z)\cap B
\]
augmented by the endpoints of \(B\), define
\[
 \widehat Q_3(t)=\frac1m\sum_{i\in F_3}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B\}
 \left[(D_i-\widehat p_-(X_i))^2\mathbf 1\{X_i<t\}
 +(D_i-\widehat p_+(X_i))^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge t\}\right]
\]
and set
\[
 \widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}=\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{t\in\mathcal T_n}\widehat Q_3(t).
\]
Thus the coarse statistic is the coefficient of a discontinuity after profiling out a continuous degree-one fit and a slope kink, while the refinement separately fits the two degree-one side regressions and classifies each observation by its residual loss.
